correctness.rationale: For any target (u,v), preimages are exactly y=u and roots of u²x³+(b−3u²)x=v−M. Differentiating gives the unique cubic threshold h=1−b/(3u²); its stationary values are ±2u²h^{3/2}. The Jacobian gives all folds and the explicit critical-value parametrization proves exactly two cusps when b>0. For b>0 the large-|x| inequality |second output|≥b|x|−|M| proves properness; for b<0 exact roots at v=M diverge as u→0. Rescaling z=|u|x gives three simple limiting zeros and the claimed uniform expansion. At b=0 y=0 collapses. The packaged check.py passed 2400 exact rational identities plus boundary/escape examples; it is a consistency check, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact b-sign threshold between proper degree-minus-one behavior and loss of two diverging inverse sheets, with full real fiber and cusp case split, is not among the examined conclusions of Wei et al., whose analytic inverse results focus on linear f and special collapse at b=0. Indexed related rational-map and piecewise-map inverse geometries have different global inverse equations and do not entail this Chebyshev-cubic transition. Generic local cusp theory only covers the local normal forms, not the sharp global b transition. Priority risk is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: Properness versus inverse branches disappearing at infinity is a global structural question in noninvertible map dynamics. The canonical Chebyshev cubic is the simplest odd two-turning-point polynomial of the source family, not an arbitrary parameter slice. One sharp b=0 wall simultaneously controls global mapping properness, cusp creation, full target-sheet multiplicity, and quantitative 1/|u| branch escape. It enables exact backward-iteration branch bookkeeping and distinguishes finite folds from nonlocal escape. The finding deliberately makes no forward attractor claims.
